text:
jamie: incident-bot triggered a pager for tenant 'SilverOak' - heartbeat check flapping, lots of pagers. paging policy says prod-critical. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: [ALERT] check=tenant-silveroak-heartbeat severity=critical count=48 window=10m link=https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/8432
jamie: I'm on it, looking at dashboard now. can someone suppress noise while we triage?
alex: oncall-rotation here, I can add a short suppression window. i'd prefer to avoid global quieting. can we target tenant filter?
jamie: yes please. heartbeat check id `tenant-silveroak-heartbeat`. A lot of the events are identical timeouts from a single region.
morgan: quick background — SilverOak started a spike in traffic yesterday and they rolled a new routing config. could be they hit a rate limiter on their side causing heartbeats to miss. SLA for SilverOak is 99.95% so we need to avoid a full-blown breach while we stabilize.
shilpa: tagging product here: we should also notify the AE. but first — reduce noise so oncall can focus.
alex: adding suppression for `check:tenant-silveroak-heartbeat` for 30m and route pages to `ops-rotation` channel only. command I used:
```
/alerts suppress --check tenant-silveroak-heartbeat --duration 30m --scope tenant:SilverOak --route ops-rotation
```
jamie: got the suppression. pages are quieting down. i'm pulling logs from the collector to confirm root cause.
jamie: logs show many 504s from SilverOak to our ingest endpoint in us-west-2 around the same timeframe. suspect intermittent NAT gateway exhaustion on their side. samples:
```
ERR conn reset by peer - upstream=ingest-01.us-west-2
[request_id=abc123] latency=512ms status=504
```
morgan: sounds likely. i'll open a low-latency channel to their SRE and ask them to check NAT/egress. can someone create a temporary per-tenant throttling rule so our backend doesn't overload?
alex: we have a per-tenant backoff available. i'll enable adaptive backoff for tenant=SilverOak for 1h. config snippet:
```
backoff:
  tenant: SilverOak
  mode: adaptive
  base_delay: 200ms
  max_delay: 5s
  duration: 1h
```
shilpa: UX note — when we do per-tenant backoffs, we should record it in the incident timeline and surface it in the console. please add an ops note.
jamie: added timeline note and linked the suppression and backoff actions. also created a temporary dashboard panel to track SilverOak heartbeat rate and error rate over 15m and 1h windows. link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/tenant-silveroak
morgan: reached out to SilverOak SRE. they're seeing bursty egress and kicked a fix to increase NAT capacity. they expect roll tomorrow morning.
jamie: with suppression + backoff + tenant fix expected, pages are manageable. we should tune the alert so it doesn't page on short bursts. proposal: change check from 3 failures in 1m to 5 failures in 5m for this tenant only.
alex: agree. i'll create a tenant-scoped alert rule instead of editing global check. new rule:
```
alert: tenant-silveroak-heartbeat-sla
expr: rate(failed_heartbeat{tenant="SilverOak"}[5m]) > 0.02
for: 5m
severity: page
route: ops-rotation
```
jamie: rolled that rule. will monitor for next 12h. also flagged this for a follow-up postmortem item: evaluate whether our default heartbeat check window is too tight for noisy tenants.
shilpa: filing a follow-up ticket: "investigate tenant-specific heartbeat sensitivity and create default per-tenant debounce policy". owners: eng-runtime + product. ETA 2 weeks.
morgan: thx all. final note before handoff to overnight oncall @ops-rotation: keep suppression off after 30m (unless we extend) and monitor SLA telemetry for SilverOak. if error budget consumption looks alarming (>0.5% over baseline) escalate to oncall manager.
ajamie: handing off to ops-rotation for overnight. summary:
- cause: customer egress/NAT constraint causing transient heartbeats
- mitigation: 30m suppression, 1h adaptive backoff, tenant-scoped alert relax to 5m window, dashboard created, SilverOak engaged
- follow-ups: postmortem ticket and per-tenant debounce policy
ops-rotation: acknowledged. will watch the dashboard overnight. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: timeline updated, incident status -> monitoring
jamie: marking this thread as resolved for active paging, leaving it open for follow-ups and the postmortem writeup. :white_check_mark:
